blocks.text: Not used yet · Ceremonial Ribbon · Quarter awards

An end-of-quarter honour recognizing effort. The teacher chooses recipients based on the effort they have shown. One to four clasp bars sit on the long center ribbon for a quarter; more clasps acknowledge greater effort. The four-clasp limit is per quarter.

Placement: Atlas/lore book. Teacher-selected end-of-quarter recognition. Up to four clasps for a quarter are displayed on the long center ribbon. Classroom award meaning assigned; automatic gameplay awarding is not implemented.
Reward: Recognition of effort through the ribbon and its clasp count. No XP, currency or stat bonus has been specified.

Fictional lore — The Divine Code: In the tradition of this ribbon, the Divine Code is a luminous pattern revealed through patient work. It becomes clearer whenever someone practices, revises, asks for help, or returns to a difficult task. Its galaxy-colored folds hold many small points of light, each recalling an attempt that mattered. The long center ribbon carries up to four clasps: visible marks of effort that has been seen and valued. The blue flower at its heart represents the understanding that grows from continuing to try. Design history: originally called Galaxy Gala; combines the Rosewater Gala layers with the Celestial Fanfare crest, pale-blue backing ribbons and blue flower brooch. The central purple tail extends slightly below the others. The number of recipients and the handling of clasps across different quarters have not been specified.
